A freed lookaside slot is not scrubbed in a release build (the 0xaa memset at src/malloc.c:461 is under SQLITE_DEBUG), so the stale byte is whatever the previous tenant left there. batch-id=fossil:19ab4811d542ba78
release_evidence: 'git log -G bSpanIsTab' gives 0dde4739f3 (2012-12-19) as the commit that added the ExprList_item.bSpanIsTab flag (documenting how zSpan is overloaded), while sqlite3ExprListDup was never updated to copy it. Fix 2c036cff3d is 2013-06-26; despite its message wondering whether it applies to trunk, the commit is an ancestor of master. 4 release tags contain the introducing commit but not the fix: version-3.7.16 (2013-03-18), 3.7.16.1 (2013-03-29), 3.7.16.2 (2013-04-12) and 3.7.17 (2013-05-20). Fixed in 3.8.0 (2013-08-26).
oracle: sqlite3ExprListDup copies items field by field and omitted bSpanIsTab, so the duplicate's flag is whatever the previous tenant left in the lookaside slot - the array comes from sqlite3DbMallocRaw and is not zeroed, and a freed slot is not scrubbed in release builds. Observable as the valgrind uninitialised-value report that found it, and potentially as mis-expansion of 'TABLE.*' result sets, since bSpanIsTab is what tells that logic how to read zSpan. No repro recorded: the fix added no test.

notes: sqlite3VdbeMemGrow(pSub, nByte, 1) was called with preserve=1 on a Mem that did not yet hold a string or blob, so the preserve path memcpy-ed pMem->n bytes from an uninitialised pMem->z. The Mem payload comes from sqlite3VdbeMemGrow -> sqlite3DbMallocRaw (src/vdbemem.c:276); an EXPLAIN sub-program list is small, so it is a lookaside slot and the copied bytes are the slot previous tenant. The fix passes nSub!=0 instead of 1, and adds assert(preserve==0 || pMem->flags&(MEM_Blob|MEM_Str)).
release_evidence: intro 165921a7427e (2009-08-28) wrote sqlite3VdbeMemGrow(pSub, nByte, 1) with a hard-coded preserve=1; blame at the fix's parent attributes that whole P4_SUBPROGRAM block to it. First released in version-3.6.18. Fix 2b9ee77fd69a (2012-03-31) changes the argument to nSub!=0 and is first contained in version-3.7.12. 24 tags, version-3.6.18 through version-3.7.11, carry the bug without the fix.
oracle: on the first P4_SUBPROGRAM operand of an EXPLAIN, when nSub is still 0, the preserve path memcpy's pMem->n bytes out of an uninitialised pMem->z into the new allocation, so the sub-program list starts with slab bytes left by the slot's previous tenant. The assert the fix adds - assert(preserve==0 || pMem->flags&(MEM_Blob|MEM_Str)) - is what fires in a SQLITE_DEBUG build. Not measured: the 2012 tree does not build with the toolchain here (lemon.c K&R declarations are rejected), and the fix added no test.

notes: A WhereTerm kept a pExpr still wrapped in TK_AS/TK_COLLATE, so later code dereferenced the node as if it were the underlying operand - a node read as the wrong shape. The fix stores sqlite3ExprSkipCollate(p) and asserts the op. Expr is 72 B from sqlite3ExprAlloc -> sqlite3DbMallocRawNN on a SELECT parse, so both nodes sit in lookaside slots and the confusion is invisible to bounds. Ticket a7b7803e8d1e869.
release_evidence: The defect belongs to the December 2012 collating-sequence rework that removed Expr.pColl (begun in ae80ddea9f, 2012-12-06) and left WhereTerm.pExpr holding TK_AS/TK_COLLATE wrappers while only exprAnalyze unwrapped them; 7a66da1395 (2012-12-07) is the first commit carrying 'sqlite3ExprSkipCollate(pTerm->pExpr)' in exprAnalyze, the call the fix deletes in favour of unwrapping once at whereClauseInsert. The CSV's be8c95ef6e9e is the branch-3.7.15 backport; the trunk fix is b290294c467b (2012-12-19), and the two diffs are byte-identical. version-3.7.15 was released 2012-12-12, inside that window, so the defect shipped; this is corroborated independently by the existence of the version-3.7.15.1 patch release (2012-12-19), which exists precisely to carry this backport and whose VERSION bump is part of the same commit.
repro_sql: CREATE TABLE t1(a,b); INSERT INTO t1 VALUES(0,'first'),(99,'fuzzy'); SELECT (t1.a==0) AS x, b FROM t1 WHERE a=0 OR x;
oracle: Segfault (upstream calls it 'the segfault problem of ticket a7b7803e8d1e869') when an AS-named result column is used as a logical term of the WHERE clause: the WhereTerm keeps an Expr still wrapped in TK_AS/TK_COLLATE and later code dereferences it as the underlying operand. Both nodes are 72-byte Expr objects in lookaside slots, so the misread stays inside the arena and can equally surface as a wrong answer rather than a fault. Correct result is '1 first'.

notes: whereClauseInsert can return 0 on failure, and the code then wrote through pWC->a[0] as if it were the new term, overwriting a live WhereTerm belonging to another clause. This is a write to the wrong element of the WhereTerm array, in bounds of the array allocation, so it is neighbour corruption inside one object. WhereTerm is 56 B and the array is allocated through the connection allocator on a SELECT parse, so it sits in a lookaside slot. Allocation site: the WhereTerm array pWC->a is grown by whereClauseInsert via sqlite3DbRealloc -> sqlite3DbMallocRawNN (src/malloc.c:643); WhereTerm is 56 B so the array sits in a 1200 B lookaside slot.
release_evidence: Intro 534230cf2e57 2011-01-22 (blame at da91e71308f8^ attributes the entire STAT2 IS-NOT-NULL block, lines 1354-1369, to it). Fix da91e71308f8 2011-02-11. Zero tagged releases contain the intro but not the fix. version-3.7.5 (2011-01-28) is date-wise between the two but does NOT contain the intro: grepping src/where.c for the control string TERM_VNULL gives 0 hits in version-3.7.4 and version-3.7.5 and 9 hits in version-3.7.6 (2011-04-12), the first release with the fix. Independently corroborated by the upstream commit message itself: 'The bug was new to the code and has not appeared in an official release. Found during structural testing.'
build_config: SQLITE_ENABLE_STAT2 (the block ends '#endif /* SQLITE_ENABLE_STAT2 */' in the fix diff)
oracle: whereClauseInsert returns 0 on allocation failure and the code then writes through pWC->a[0] as if it were the new term, overwriting a live WhereTerm belonging to another clause. This is a write to the wrong element of an in-bounds array, so it is neighbour corruption inside one 1200-byte lookaside slot: expect a wrong query plan or a segfault under OOM injection, and NO ASAN report even with lookaside disabled, since the write stays within the array allocation. Reachable only on the OOM path, which is why upstream found it by structural testing rather than by a query. No trigger recorded: the fix added no test and no PoC exists.

notes: Mem payload pOut->zMalloc from sqlite3VdbeMemGrow -> sqlite3DbMallocRaw, src/vdbemem.c:276; a UTF16-converted string literal is well under the 1200 B slot so it is a lookaside slot. Freed twice = the same slot pushed onto db->lookaside.pFree twice (src/malloc.c:481), so two later allocations alias one slot. No free() reaches the system allocator, so revocation never runs.
release_evidence: git log -L over the too_big check inside the OP_String8 UTF16 branch shows bb4957f85812 (2008-03-20, 'Initial implementation of per-connection limits and the sqlite3_limit() API') replacing 'pOp->p1>SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH' with 'pOp->p1>db->aLimit[SQLITE_LIMIT_LENGTH]'. That is what makes the trigger named in the fix's own message - changing SQLITE_LIMIT_LENGTH after prepare but before step - reachable at all; with the compile-time constant the branch could not be taken after the P4 had been rewritten. Intro first released in version-3.5.8; fix 3a9cf17d7c5a (2009-06-17) first contained in version-3.6.16. 22 tags, version-3.5.8 through version-3.6.15, carry the bug without the fix.
build_config: default; needs !SQLITE_OMIT_UTF16 and a UTF-16 connection encoding
oracle: the Mem payload of the UTF16-converted literal is handed both to pOp->p4.z as P4_DYNAMIC and to the output register, and the too_big exit then frees it twice - the same lookaside slot pushed onto db->lookaside.pFree twice, so two later allocations alias one slot. No SQL-only trigger: it needs sqlite3_limit(db, SQLITE_LIMIT_LENGTH, n) called between sqlite3_prepare_v2() and sqlite3_step(). The fix added no test - its only test-file change removes debug pragmas from tkt3841.test.

notes: READ_UTF16LE/READ_UTF16BE consume 2 more bytes past zTerm when the buffer ends on the first half of a surrogate pair (src/utf.c:242 and :551 in 3.53.4). The buffer is Mem.z, allocated by sqlite3VdbeMemGrow -> sqlite3DbMallocRaw(pMem->db,n) (src/vdbemem.c:276) with a 32-byte floor; n<=1200 gives a lookaside big slot (n<=128 a 128-byte small slot), so 2 bytes past a short string stay inside the slot. A UTF-16 value longer than 1200 bytes, or an application buffer bound with SQLITE_STATIC or a destructor, is outside the arena and would be caught. batch-id=fossil:19064d7cea838e1a
release_evidence: git blame of the READ_UTF16LE/READ_UTF16BE macros at src/utf.c:110-118 @7c95b0f3dab6^ gives bfd6cce56bb (2004-06-18), which wrote them consuming a second code unit for a surrogate pair with no zTerm bound - the parameter the fix adds. The one later commit touching those lines, 769e97e0323 (2009-04-01), was checked and only deletes dead code ('if((c&0xFFFF0000)==0) c=0xFFFD;') and fixes whitespace, so it is not the introducer. Fix 7c95b0f3da is 2009-10-23. 82 release tags contain the introducing commit but not the fix, from version-3.0.0 (2004-06-18, the same day) through version-3.6.19 (2009-10-14); fixed in 3.6.20 (2009-11-04).
build_config: default to trigger; the regression test additionally needs an SQLITE_TEST build, because hex_to_utf16be/hex_to_utf16le are test-only functions added to src/test_func.c by this same commit
repro_sql: PRAGMA encoding=UTF8; CREATE TABLE t1(x); INSERT INTO t1 VALUES(hex_to_utf16be('D800')); SELECT hex(x) FROM t1;
oracle: Correct output is EDA080 (U+FFFD-style replacement encoding of the lone surrogate); before the fix READ_UTF16 consumes 2 bytes past zTerm when the buffer ends on the first half of a surrogate pair, so the decoded character - and hence the hex() output - is built from whatever follows the string. The buffer is Mem.z from sqlite3VdbeMemGrow with a 32-byte floor, so for short strings the overread stays inside the lookaside slot and is silent; an ASAN heap-buffer-overflow read needs a UTF-16 value over 1200 bytes, an application buffer bound with SQLITE_STATIC, or lookaside disabled.

notes: pParse->aAlias was allocated for the alias count known at the time but never tracked how many slots were actually allocated, so a later nested VIEW wrote past the array; the fix adds Parse.nAliasAlloc and reallocs. Ticket #3527. aAlias is grown with sqlite3DbReallocOrFree and is a small pointer array, so it occupies a lookaside slot and the overrun lands in the neighbouring slot. Lookaside is present at this revision - verified by reading src/sqliteInt.h AT the commit (23 occurrences; positive control: master shows 68, and the 2008-04 tree shows 0), so the arena existed when this bug shipped. Allocation site: sqlite3DbReallocOrFree -> sqlite3DbMallocRawNN (src/malloc.c:643); a small pointer array, so a lookaside slot.
release_evidence: Intro 8b213899e804 2008-08-29, which added codeAlias and the Parse.aAlias array allocated for the then-known alias count (blame at 555f8de7ef22^ attributes the 'if( pParse->aAlias==0 )' block and the nAlias/aAlias struct members to it). Fix 555f8de7ef22 2008-12-08, which adds Parse.nAliasAlloc and reallocs. 7 tagged releases contain the intro but not the fix, version-3.6.2 (2008-08-30) through version-3.6.6.2 (2008-11-26). Fix first in version-3.6.7 (2008-12-16).
repro_sql: CREATE TABLE Element ( Code INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, Name VARCHAR(60) ); CREATE TABLE ElemOr ( CodeOr INTEGER NOT NULL, Code INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(CodeOr,Code) ); CREATE TABLE ElemAnd ( CodeAnd INTEGER, Code INTEGER, Attr1 INTEGER, Attr2 INTEGER, Attr3 INTEGER, PRIMARY KEY(CodeAnd,Code) ); INSERT INTO Element VALUES(1,'Elem1'); INSERT INTO Element VALUES(2,'Elem2'); INSERT INTO Element VALUES(3,'Elem3'); INSERT INTO Element VALUES(4,'Elem4'); INSERT INTO Element VALUES(5,'Elem5'); INSERT INTO ElemOr Values(3,4); INSERT INTO ElemOr Values(3,5); INSERT INTO ElemAnd VALUES(1,3,1,1,1); INSERT INTO ElemAnd VALUES(1,2,1,1,1); CREATE VIEW ElemView1 AS SELECT CAST(Element.Code AS VARCHAR(50)) AS ElemId, Element.Code AS ElemCode, Element.Name AS ElemName, ElemAnd.Code AS InnerCode, ElemAnd.Attr1 AS Attr1, ElemAnd.Attr2 AS Attr2, ElemAnd.Attr3 AS Attr3, 0 AS Level, 0 AS IsOrElem FROM Element JOIN ElemAnd ON ElemAnd.CodeAnd=Element.Code WHERE ElemAnd.CodeAnd NOT IN (SELECT CodeOr FROM ElemOr) UNION ALL SELECT CAST(ElemOr.CodeOr AS VARCHAR(50)) AS ElemId, Element.Code AS ElemCode, Element.Name AS ElemName, ElemOr.Code AS InnerCode, NULL AS Attr1, NULL AS Attr2, NULL AS Attr3, 0 AS Level, 1 AS IsOrElem FROM ElemOr JOIN Element ON Element.Code=ElemOr.CodeOr ORDER BY ElemId, InnerCode; CREATE VIEW ElemView2 AS SELECT ElemId, ElemCode, ElemName, InnerCode, Attr1, Attr2, Attr3, Level, IsOrElem FROM ElemView1 UNION ALL SELECT Element.ElemId || '.' || InnerElem.ElemId AS ElemId, InnerElem.ElemCode, InnerElem.ElemName, InnerElem.InnerCode, InnerElem.Attr1, InnerElem.Attr2, InnerElem.Attr3, InnerElem.Level+1, InnerElem.IsOrElem FROM ElemView1 AS Element JOIN ElemView1 AS InnerElem ON Element.Level=0 AND Element.InnerCode=InnerElem.ElemCode ORDER BY ElemId, InnerCode; SELECT * FROM ElemView1;
oracle: Upstream test expects {1 1 Elem1 2 1 1 1 0 0 1 1 Elem1 3 1 1 1 0 0 3 3 Elem3 4 {} {} {} 0 1 3 3 Elem3 5 {} {} {} 0 1} for 1.1 and a longer row set for 1.2 (SELECT * FROM ElemView2, the nested-VIEW case that actually overruns). A later nested VIEW raises pParse->nAlias above the count aAlias was sized for, so codeAlias writes past the array. It is a small pointer array in a lookaside slot, so the overrun lands in the neighbouring slot: expect a segfault (upstream called it one) or corrupted register numbers giving a wrong answer, with an ASAN heap-buffer-overflow WRITE only when lookaside is disabled.

notes: Malformed UTF16 with an odd byte count let the converter run zTerm past the end of the input; the fix masks pMem->n with ~1. Ticket #3482. The input is a Mem text payload from sqlite3VdbeMemGrow -> sqlite3DbMallocRaw, so a string under the slot size lives in a lookaside slot and the overrun stays inside the connection slab. Lookaside is present at this revision - verified by reading src/sqliteInt.h AT the commit (23 occurrences; positive control: master shows 68, and the 2008-04 tree shows 0), so the arena existed when this bug shipped.
release_evidence: intro bfd6cce56bbb (2004-06-18) wrote 'zTerm = &zIn[pMem->n]' with no odd-length guard in the UTF-16 byte-swap loop of sqlite3VdbeMemTranslate; blame at the fix's parent still attributes that line to it. First released in version-3.0.0. Fix bbf695d6ead1 (2008-11-07, ticket #3482) masks pMem->n with ~1 and is first contained in version-3.6.5. 62 tags, version-3.0.0 through version-3.6.4, carry the bug without the fix.
repro_sql: PRAGMA encoding=UTF16be; SELECT hex(ltrim(x'6efcda'));
oracle: MEASURED at bbf695d6ead1^: returns 6EFCDA00DD7D - six bytes where two (6EFC) are correct - and the four extra bytes CHANGE between runs of the same binary (6EFCDA00DEBE on the next run), which is recycled slab content appearing directly in the query result. Post-fix returns 6EFC. Silent in both lookaside arms with no ASAN report, because the overrun stays inside the connection slab.
